question: Should this PR intentionally make unsafe numeric byte-size values in existing agent compaction config fail validation?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but root policy treats stricter validation of existing config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive because upgrades can expose the change at config load time.

options.title: Accept strict unsafe rejection
options.body: Merge the PR with the explicit decision that values JavaScript cannot represent exactly are invalid config, even if earlier builds accepted them.

options.title: Require upgrade mitigation
options.body: Ask for a short PR-body/docs note or doctor strategy before merge if maintainers want operator-facing upgrade guidance for this edge case.

options.title: Preserve legacy acceptance
options.body: Pause this direction if maintainers want unsafe numeric values to keep loading, though that would preserve precision-corrupted byte counts.

recommendation.title: Accept strict unsafe rejection
recommendation.body: Merge the PR with the explicit decision that values JavaScript cannot represent exactly are invalid config, even if earlier builds accepted them.
